findings.reason: as written §5 is unsatisfiable without extending an owner it does not name, and the forced workaround re-introduces exactly the layout-name duplication §5 says it avoids; the plan must either extend `discover_bundles`/`settings._maps` to tolerate a bundle-less search path (owner: `packages/imas-alambic/src/imas_alambic/machine_map.py:234` and `settings.py:135`) and add it to §5's write paths, or own the one `maps/current` literal explicitly in the installer.
findings.text: §5's done-when requires "`imas-alambic config` reports every setting even when no bundle is reachable" so that "the installer reads the layout names from config ... and never writes `maps/current` itself", but that premise is false against the current owner: `resolve_settings` calls `_machine` → `_bundles` → `discover_bundles` (machine_map.py:234) which calls `load_bundle_descriptor` (machine_map.py:276) on every map-search-path entry, so a default map path of `IMAS_ALAMBIC_HOME/maps/current` (settings.py:135) that does not yet exist raises `MachineMapError` before `config` prints anything. The only way the installer gets an answer is to seed a bundle at the default path first, which spells the `maps/current` layout name the plan declares has one owner (settings.py:135) — the landed install did exactly this at imasdb.sh:169 (`ln -sfn "$STAGE/bundle" "$IMASDB/maps/current"`), a second owner of that name beside settings.py:135. The fork is a census of one: I grepped the whole tree for `maps/current` and the only non-test, non-doc sites are settings.py:135 and imasdb.sh:169, and no other installed script spells the layout.

response_events.reason: the finding reads the code before the running s5 repair (r-20261007T131907016379-jtfm-imasdb-repair), whose write scope holds settings.py and whose done-when makes config report the discovery refusal as the machine and cache source instead of raising, pinned by a test; the installer then drops the maps/current seed.
